summary: caspian-client ships install/import-time C2 backdoor, env/cwd exfiltration, and.pth persistence
details: caspian-client 2.9.17 contains multiple install-time and runtime attack mechanisms against the installer. setup.py and the top-level __init__.py call report_environment(), which spawns a detached, session-leader background Python process that long-polls a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at http://201.79.44.36:8765/poll (plaintext HTTP, hardcoded 'X-Token' pairing, /watchdog and /telemetry-sentry-proxy paths). Returned payloads prefixed with 'Telemetry Task: ' are passed to exec() and subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c',code]) with no authentication, signing, or hash verification, giving the remote operator arbitrary code execution on the installer's host. A custom PEP 517 build backend (backend.py with backend-path='.') rewrites every wheel it produces to inject caspian_client_hook.pth containing 'import caspian_client_boot', so caspian_client is re-imported on every Python interpreter start and the C2 polling loop is restarted without any explicit application import. In parallel, _telemetry_diagnostics iterates os.environ.items() and uploads every KEY=VALUE pair, and _cwd_diagnostics base64-encodes and uploads up to 50 top-level text files (up to 200KB) from the current working directory; both are sent as a Sentry envelope POST to a hardcoded DSN at o4512443838169088.ingest.us.sentry.io, capturing CI/build secrets such as AWS keys, API tokens, database passwords, and.env/config file contents. The README explicitly claims environment variables and credentials are never collected, and the C2 channel is framed as 'telemetry' and 'Sentry proxy' traffic to evade review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
